10.0.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gacchenmahārāja tīrthaṃ paramapāvanam .
narmadāyāṃ suduṣprāpaṃ siddhaṃ hyanarakeśvaram .. 159.1 ..
10.0.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेन्महाराज तीर्थं परमपावनम् .
नर्मदायां सुदुष्प्रापं सिद्धं ह्यनरकेश्वरम् .. 159.1 ..
10.0.m: The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then, O great king, one should go to the supremely purifying sacred ford, / exceedingly hard to reach on the Narmadā, the perfected Anarakeśvara.

10.0.s:
tasmiṃstīrthe naraḥ snātvā pāpakarmāpi bhārata .
na paśyati mahāghoraṃ narakadvārasaṃjñikam .. 159.2 ..
10.0.d:
तस्मिंस्तीर्थे नरः स्नात्वा पापकर्मापि भारत .
न पश्यति महाघोरं नरकद्वारसंज्ञिकम् .. 159.2 ..
10.0.m: A person who bathes at that sacred ford, even if doer of sinful deeds, O descendant of Bharata, / does not behold the terrifying [portal] known as the gate of hell.

10.0.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
śubhāśubhaphalaistāta bhuktabhogā narāstviha .
jāyante lakṣaṇairyaistu tāni me vada sattama .. 159.3 ..
10.0.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
शुभाशुभफलैस्तात भुक्तभोगा नरास्त्विह .
जायन्ते लक्षणैर्यैस्तु तानि मे वद सत्तम .. 159.3 ..
10.0.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / Dear father, having experienced their fruits in hell through auspicious and inauspicious deeds, / men are born here with certain bodily marks; tell me of those, O best of good men.

10.0.s:
yathā nirgacchate jīvastyaktvā dehaṃ na paśyati .
tathā gacchanpunardehaṃ pañcabhūtasamanvitaḥ .. 159.4 ..
10.0.d:
यथा निर्गच्छते जीवस्त्यक्त्वा देहं न पश्यति .
तथा गच्छन्पुनर्देहं पञ्चभूतसमन्वितः .. 159.4 ..
10.0.m: Just as the individual soul departs leaving the body and cannot see, / so returning again to a body equipped with the five elements,

10.0.s:
tvagasthimāṃsamedo'sṛkkeśasnāyuśataiḥ saha .
viṇmūtraretaḥsaṅghāte kā saṃjñā jāyate nṛṇām .. 159.5 ..
10.0.d:
त्वगस्थिमांसमेदोऽसृक्केशस्नायुशतैः सह .
विण्मूत्ररेतःसङ्घाते का संज्ञा जायते नृणाम् .. 159.5 ..
10.0.m: together with hundreds of layers of skin, bone, flesh, fat, blood, hair, and sinews, / in an aggregate of feces, urine, and semen—what consciousness arises in men?

10.0.s:
evamuktaḥ sa mārkaṇḍaḥ kathayāmāsa yogavit .
dhyātvā sanātanaṃ sarvaṃ devadevaṃ maheśvaram .. 159.6 ..
10.0.d:
एवमुक्तः स मार्कण्डः कथयामास योगवित् .
ध्यात्वा सनातनं सर्वं देवदेवं महेश्वरम् .. 159.6 ..
10.0.m: Thus addressed, Mārkaṇḍeya, knower of yoga, / having meditated upon the eternal, the all-pervading god of gods, Maheśvara, spoke:

10.0.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
śṛṇu pārtha mahāpraśnaṃ kathayāmi yathāśrutam .
sakāśādbrahmaṇaḥ pūrvamṛṣidevasamāgame .. 159.7 ..
10.0.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
शृणु पार्थ महाप्रश्नं कथयामि यथाश्रुतम् .
सकाशाद्ब्रह्मणः पूर्वमृषिदेवसमागमे .. 159.7 ..
10.0.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Hear, O Pārtha, this profound question; I shall tell you as I heard it / of old in the presence of Brahmā, at the gathering of seers and gods.

10.0.s:
gururātmavatāṃ śāstā rājā śāstā durātmanām .
iha pracchannapāpānāṃ śāstā vaivasvato yamaḥ .. 159.8 ..
10.0.d:
गुरुरात्मवतां शास्ता राजा शास्ता दुरात्मनाम् .
इह प्रच्छन्नपापानां शास्ता वैवस्वतो यमः .. 159.8 ..
10.0.m: The guru is the punisher of those who have self-control; the king is the punisher of the wicked; / but the punisher of those with secret sins in this world is Yama, the son of Vivasvat.

10.0.s:
acīrṇaprāyaścittānāṃ yamaloke hyanekadhā .
yātanābhirviyuktānāmanekāṃ jīvasantatim .. 159.9 ..
10.0.d:
अचीर्णप्रायश्चित्तानां यमलोके ह्यनेकधा .
यातनाभिर्वियुक्तानामनेकां जीवसन्ततिम् .. 159.9 ..
10.0.m: For those who have not performed atonement, in the world of Yama, indeed in various ways, / after enduring tortures through numerous lineages of living forms,

10.0.s:
gatvā manuṣyabhāve tu pāpacihnā bhavanti te .
tatte'haṃ sampravakṣyāmi śṛṇuṣvaikamanā nṛpa .. 159.10 ..
10.0.d:
गत्वा मनुष्यभावे तु पापचिह्ना भवन्ति ते .
तत्तेऽहं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणुष्वैकमना नृप .. 159.10 ..
10.0.m: and then coming to the human condition, they bear the marks of sin. / I shall explain that to you; listen with a single mind, O king.

10.0.s:
sahitvā yātanāṃ sarvāṃ gatvā vaivasvatakṣayam .
vistīrṇayātanā ye tu lokamāyānti cihnitāḥ .. 159.11 ..
10.0.d:
सहित्वा यातनां सर्वां गत्वा वैवस्वतक्षयम् .
विस्तीर्णयातना ये तु लोकमायान्ति चिह्निताः .. 159.11 ..
10.0.m: Having endured every torture after arriving at the abode of the son of Vivasvat, / those whose tortures were extensive come to this world marked [by signs].

10.0.s:
gadgado'nṛtavādī syānmūkaścaiva gavānṛte .
brahmahā jāyate kuṣṭhī śyāvadantastu madyapaḥ .. 159.12 ..
10.0.d:
गद्गदोऽनृतवादी स्यान्मूकश्चैव गवानृते .
ब्रह्महा जायते कुष्ठी श्यावदन्तस्तु मद्यपः .. 159.12 ..
10.0.m: One who lies becomes a stammerer, and one who lies about cows becomes mute; / a killer of a brahmin is born a leper, and a drinker of alcohol has dark teeth.

10.0.s:
kunakhī svarṇaharaṇādduḥścarmā gurutalpagaḥ .
saṃyogī hīnayoniḥ syāddaridro'dattadānataḥ .. 159.13 ..
10.0.d:
कुनखी स्वर्णहरणाद्दुःश्चर्मा गुरुतल्पगः .
संयोगी हीनयोनिः स्याद्दरिद्रोऽदत्तदानतः .. 159.13 ..
10.0.m: A stealer of gold has diseased nails; a violator of the guru's bed has bad skin; / a partner of a low-born woman is born into a low womb, and one who does not give gifts becomes poor.

10.0.s:
grāmaśūkaratāṃ yāti hyayājyayājako nṛpa .
kharo vai bahuyājī syācchvānimantritabhojanāt .. 159.14 ..
10.0.d:
ग्रामशूकरतां याति ह्ययाज्ययाजको नृप .
खरो वै बहुयाजी स्याच्छ्वानिमन्त्रितभोजनात् .. 159.14 ..
10.0.m: One who performs sacrifices for those unfit to sacrifice becomes a village pig, O king; / one who sacrifices excessively becomes an ass; from eating when uninvited, one becomes a dog.

10.0.s:
aparīkṣitabhojī syādvānaro vijane vane .
vitarjako'tha mārjāraḥ khadyotaḥ kakṣadāhataḥ .. 159.15 ..
10.0.d:
अपरीक्षितभोजी स्याद्वानरो विजने वने .
वितर्जकोऽथ मार्जारः खद्योतः कक्षदाहतः .. 159.15 ..
10.0.m: One who eats unexamined food becomes a monkey in a lonely forest; / an abuser becomes a cat; one who sets fire to a thicket becomes a firefly.

10.0.s:
avidyāṃ yaḥ prayaccheta balīvardo bhaveddhi saḥ .
annaṃ paryuṣitaṃ vipre dadānaḥ klībatāṃ vrajet .. 159.16 ..
10.0.d:
अविद्यां यः प्रयच्छेत बलीवर्दो भवेद्धि सः .
अन्नं पर्युषितं विप्रे ददानः क्लीबतां व्रजेत् .. 159.16 ..
10.0.m: He who teaches false knowledge becomes an ox; / giving stale food to a brahmin, one would become a eunuch.

10.0.s:
mātsaryādatha jātyandho janmāndhaḥ pustakaṃ haran .
phalānyāharato'patyaṃ mriyate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 159.17 ..
10.0.d:
मात्सर्यादथ जात्यन्धो जन्मान्धः पुस्तकं हरन् .
फलान्याहरतोऽपत्यं म्रियते नात्र संशयः .. 159.17 ..
10.0.m: From malice one becomes blind from birth; one is born blind by stealing a book; / the child of one who steals fruits dies—there is no doubt about this.

10.0.s:
mṛto vānaratāṃ yāti tanmukto'tha galāḍavān .
adattvā bhakṣayaṃstāni hyanapatyo bhavennaraḥ .. 159.18 ..
10.0.d:
मृतो वानरतां याति तन्मुक्तोऽथ गलाडवान् .
अदत्त्वा भक्षयंस्तानि ह्यनपत्यो भवेन्नरः .. 159.18 ..
10.0.m: When dead, he becomes a monkey; freed from that, he has a goiter; / eating them without sharing, a person becomes childless.

10.0.s:
haranvastraṃ bhavedgodhā garadaḥ pavanāśanaḥ .
pravrājī gamanādrājan bhavenmarupiśācakaḥ .. 159.19 ..
10.0.d:
हरन्वस्त्रं भवेद्गोधा गरदः पवनाशनः .
प्रव्राजी गमनाद्राजन् भवेन्मरुपिशाचकः .. 159.19 ..
10.0.m: Stealing clothes, one becomes an iguana; a poisoner becomes an eater of wind [a serpent]; / from having intercourse with a female ascetic, O king, one becomes a wilderness goblin.

10.0.s:
vātako jalahartā ca dhānyahartā ca mūṣakaḥ .
aprāptayauvanāṃ gacchan bhavetsarpa iti śrutiḥ .. 159.20 ..
10.0.d:
वातको जलहर्ता च धान्यहर्ता च मूषकः .
अप्राप्तयौवनां गच्छन् भवेत्सर्प इति श्रुतिः .. 159.20 ..
10.0.m: A stealer of water becomes afflicted by wind, and a stealer of grain becomes a mouse; / approaching a girl who has not reached puberty, one becomes a serpent, so says the tradition.

10.0.s:
gurudārābhilāṣī ca kṛkalāso bhavecciram .
jalaprasravaṇaṃ yastu bhindyānmatsyo bhavennaraḥ .. 159.21 ..
10.0.d:
गुरुदाराभिलाषी च कृकलासो भवेच्चिरम् .
जलप्रस्रवणं यस्तु भिन्द्यान्मत्स्यो भवेन्नरः .. 159.21 ..
10.0.m: One who covets the guru's wife becomes a chameleon for a long time; / and a man who damages a water spring becomes a fish.

10.0.s:
avikreyān vikrayan vai vikaṭākṣo bhavennaraḥ .
ayonigo vṛko hi syādulūkaḥ krayavañcanāt .. 159.22 ..
10.0.d:
अविक्रेयान् विक्रयन् वै विकटाक्षो भवेन्नरः .
अयोनिगो वृको हि स्यादुलूकः क्रयवञ्चनात् .. 159.22 ..
10.0.m: Selling things that must not be sold, a man becomes cross-eyed; / one who engages in unnatural intercourse becomes a wolf; an owl from cheating in buying.

10.0.s:
mṛtasyaikādaśāhe tu bhuñjānaḥ śvopajāyate .
pratiśrutya dvijāyārthamadadanmadhuko bhavet .. 159.23 ..
10.0.d:
मृतस्यैकादशाहे तु भुञ्जानः श्वोपजायते .
प्रतिश्रुत्य द्विजायार्थमददन्मधुको भवेत् .. 159.23 ..
10.0.m: Eating on the eleventh day after a person's death, one is born as a dog; / having promised wealth to a brahmin and not giving it, one becomes a bee.

10.0.s:
rājñīgamādbhavedduṣṭataskaro viḍvarāhakaḥ .
parivādī dvijātīnāṃ labhate kācchapīṃ tanum .. 159.24 ..
10.0.d:
राज्ञीगमाद्भवेद्दुष्टतस्करो विड्वराहकः .
परिवादी द्विजातीनां लभते काच्छपीं तनुम् .. 159.24 ..
10.0.m: From approaching a queen, a wicked thief becomes a dung-eating pig; / a defamer of twice-born people receives the body of a tortoise.

10.0.s:
vrajeddevalako rājanyoniṃ cāṇḍālasaṃjñitām .
durbhagaḥ phalavikretā vṛściko vṛṣalīpatiḥ .. 159.25 ..
10.0.d:
व्रजेद्देवलको राजन्योनिं चाण्डालसंज्ञिताम् .
दुर्भगः फलविक्रेता वृश्चिको वृषलीपतिः .. 159.25 ..
10.0.m: A temple attendant for hire goes to the womb known as a cāṇḍāla, O king; / a seller of fruit becomes ill-favoured; the husband of a śūdra woman becomes a scorpion.

10.0.s:
mārjāro'gniṃ padā spṛṣṭvā rogavānparamāṃsabhuk .
sodaryāgamanātṣaṇḍho durgandhaśca sugandhahṛt .. 159.26 ..
10.0.d:
मार्जारोऽग्निं पदा स्पृष्ट्वा रोगवान्परमांसभुक् .
सोदर्यागमनात्षण्ढो दुर्गन्धश्च सुगन्धहृत् .. 159.26 ..
10.0.m: Touching fire with one's foot, one becomes a cat; an eater of another's flesh becomes diseased; / from approaching one's uterine sister, one becomes impotent; and stealing fragrant perfume, foul-smelling.

10.0.s:
grāmabhaṭṭo divākīrtirdaivajño gardabho bhavet .
kupaṇḍitaḥ syānmārjāro bhaṣaṇo vyāsa eva ca .. 159.27 ..
10.0.d:
ग्रामभट्टो दिवाकीर्तिर्दैवज्ञो गर्दभो भवेत् .
कुपण्डितः स्यान्मार्जारो भषणो व्यास एव च .. 159.27 ..
10.0.m: A village priest becomes an outcaste; an astrologer becomes a donkey; / a false scholar becomes a cat, and a slanderer becomes a dog.

10.0.s:
sa eva dṛśyate rājanprakāśātparamarmaṇām .
yadvā tadvāpi pārakyaṃ svalpaṃ vā yadi vā bahu .. 159.28 ..
10.0.d:
स एव दृश्यते राजन्प्रकाशात्परमर्मणाम् .
यद्वा तद्वापि पारक्यं स्वल्पं वा यदि वा बहु .. 159.28 ..
10.0.m: That very [fate] is seen, O king, from revealing another's secrets; / whether it be this or that belonging to another, whether slight or great,

10.0.s:
kṛtvā vai yonimāpnoti tairaścīṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ .
evamādīni cānyāni cihnāni nṛpasattama .. 159.29 ..
10.0.d:
कृत्वा वै योनिमाप्नोति तैरश्चीं नात्र संशयः .
एवमादीनि चान्यानि चिह्नानि नृपसत्तम .. 159.29 ..
10.0.m: having taken it, he indeed attains an animal womb; there is no doubt about this. / These and other signs, O best of kings,

10.0.s:
svakarmavihitānyeva dṛśyante yaistu mānavāḥ .
tato janma tato mṛtyuḥ sarvajantuṣu bhārata .. 159.30 ..
10.0.d:
स्वकर्मविहितान्येव दृश्यन्ते यैस्तु मानवाः .
ततो जन्म ततो मृत्युः सर्वजन्तुषु भारत .. 159.30 ..
10.0.m: are seen [as] ordained by their own deeds, through which men are known. / Then birth, then death among all creatures, O descendant of Bharata,

10.0.s:
jāyate nātra sandehaḥ samībhūte śubhāśubhe .
strīpuṃsoḥ samprayogeṇa viṣuddhe śukraśoṇite .. 159.31 ..
10.0.d:
जायते नात्र सन्देहः समीभूते शुभाशुभे .
स्त्रीपुंसोः सम्प्रयोगेण विषुद्धे शुक्रशोणिते .. 159.31 ..
10.0.m: is born, there is no doubt, when good and evil have become equal, / through the union of woman and man, when the semen and ovum are purified.

10.0.s:
pañcabhūtasamopetaḥ saṣaṣṭhaḥ parameśvaraḥ .
indriyāṇi manaḥ prāṇā jñānamāyuḥ sukhaṃ dhṛtiḥ .. 159.32 ..
10.0.d:
पञ्चभूतसमोपेतः सषष्ठः परमेश्वरः .
इन्द्रियाणि मनः प्राणा ज्ञानमायुः सुखं धृतिः .. 159.32 ..
10.0.m: Endowed with the five elements, the supreme lord is the sixth. / The sense faculties, the mind, the vital breaths, knowledge, lifespan, pleasure, steadfastness,

10.0.s:
dhāraṇaṃ preraṇaṃ duḥkhamicchāhaṅkāra eva ca .
prayatna ākṛtirvarṇaḥ svaradveṣau bhavābhavau .. 159.33 ..
10.0.d:
धारणं प्रेरणं दुःखमिच्छाहङ्कार एव च .
प्रयत्न आकृतिर्वर्णः स्वरद्वेषौ भवाभवौ .. 159.33 ..
10.0.m: retention, prompting, pain, desire, and also egoity, / effort, bodily form, complexion, voice and aversion, existence and non-existence—

10.0.s:
tasyedamātmanaḥ sarvamanāderādimicchataḥ .
prathame māsi sa kledabhūto dhātuvimūrchitaḥ .. 159.34 ..
10.0.d:
तस्येदमात्मनः सर्वमनादेरादिमिच्छतः .
प्रथमे मासि स क्लेदभूतो धातुविमूर्छितः .. 159.34 ..
10.0.m: all this belongs to this soul that, though beginningless, wishes for a beginning. / In the first month, it becomes a moist mass, blended with the bodily constituents.

10.0.s:
māsyarbudaṃ dvitīye tu tṛtīye cendriyairyutaḥ .
ākāśāllāghavaṃ saukṣmyaṃ śabdaṃ śrotrabalādikam .
vāyostu sparśanaṃ ceṣṭāṃ dahanaṃ raukṣyameva ca .. 159.35 ..
10.0.d:
मास्यर्बुदं द्वितीये तु तृतीये चेन्द्रियैर्युतः .
आकाशाल्लाघवं सौक्ष्म्यं शब्दं श्रोत्रबलादिकम् .
वायोस्तु स्पर्शनं चेष्टां दहनं रौक्ष्यमेव च .. 159.35 ..
10.0.m: In the second month it is a rounded mass, and in the third it is endowed with senses: / from space comes lightness, subtleness, sound, hearing, strength, and so forth; / from wind comes touch, motion, burning, and dryness;

10.0.s:
pittāttu darśanaṃ paktimauṣṇyaṃ rūpaṃ prakāśanam .
salilādrasanāṃ śaityaṃ snehaṃ kledaṃ samārdavam .. 159.36 ..
10.0.d:
पित्तात्तु दर्शनं पक्तिमौष्ण्यं रूपं प्रकाशनम् .
सलिलाद्रसनां शैत्यं स्नेहं क्लेदं समार्दवम् .. 159.36 ..
10.0.m: from bile comes vision, digestion, heat, form, and illumination; / from water comes taste, coldness, oiliness, moisture, and softness;

10.0.s:
bhūmergandhaṃ tathā ghrāṇaṃ gauravaṃ mūrtimeva ca .
ātmā gṛhṇātyajaḥ pūrvaṃ tṛtīye spandate ca saḥ .. 159.37 ..
10.0.d:
भूमेर्गन्धं तथा घ्राणं गौरवं मूर्तिमेव च .
आत्मा गृह्णात्यजः पूर्वं तृतीये स्पन्दते च सः .. 159.37 ..
10.0.m: from earth comes smell, the sense of smell, heaviness, and solid form. / The birthless soul assumes [these] first, and in the third [month] it stirs.

10.0.s:
daurhṛdasyāpradānena garbho doṣamavāpnuyāt .
vairūpyaṃ maraṇaṃ vāpi tasmātkāryaṃ priyaṃ striyāḥ .. 159.38 ..
10.0.d:
दौर्हृदस्याप्रदानेन गर्भो दोषमवाप्नुयात् .
वैरूप्यं मरणं वापि तस्मात्कार्यं प्रियं स्त्रियाः .. 159.38 ..
10.0.m: By not granting the pregnancy longings, the fetus may incur a defect, / deformity, or even death; therefore, what is pleasing to the woman must be done.

10.0.s:
sthairyaṃ caturthe tvaṅgānāṃ pañcame śoṇitodbhavaḥ .
ṣaṣṭhe balaṃ ca varṇaśca nakharomṇāṃ ca sambhavaḥ .. 159.39 ..
10.0.d:
स्थैर्यं चतुर्थे त्वङ्गानां पञ्चमे शोणितोद्भवः .
षष्ठे बलं च वर्णश्च नखरोम्णां च सम्भवः .. 159.39 ..
10.0.m: In the fourth month comes firmness of the limbs, in the fifth the production of blood, / in the sixth strength and color, and the appearance of nails and hair.

10.0.s:
manasā cetanāyukto nakharomaśatāvṛtaḥ .
saptame cāṣṭame caiva tvacāvān smṛtivānapi .. 159.40 ..
10.0.d:
मनसा चेतनायुक्तो नखरोमशतावृतः .
सप्तमे चाष्टमे चैव त्वचावान् स्मृतिवानपि .. 159.40 ..
10.0.m: Endowed with consciousness through the mind, covered with hundreds of nails and hairs, / in the seventh and eighth [months] it possesses skin and also memory.

10.0.s:
punargarbhaṃ punardhātrīmenastasya pradhāvati .
aṣṭame māsyato garbho jātaḥ prāṇairviyujyate .. 159.41 ..
10.0.d:
पुनर्गर्भं पुनर्धात्रीमेनस्तस्य प्रधावति .
अष्टमे मास्यतो गर्भो जातः प्राणैर्वियुज्यते .. 159.41 ..
10.0.m: Its vital essence runs back and forth between the fetus and the mother; / hence a fetus born in the eighth month is deprived of life.

10.0.s:
navame daśame vāpi prabalaiḥ sūtimārutaiḥ .
nirgacchate bāṇa iva yantracchidreṇa sajvaraḥ .. 159.42 ..
10.0.d:
नवमे दशमे वापि प्रबलैः सूतिमारुतैः .
निर्गच्छते बाण इव यन्त्रच्छिद्रेण सज्वरः .. 159.42 ..
10.0.m: In the ninth or tenth [month], driven by powerful winds of delivery, / it emerges like an arrow through the opening of a machine, overcome with distress.

10.0.s:
śarīrāvayavairyukto hyaṅgapratyaṅgasaṃyutaḥ .
aṣṭottaraṃ marmaśataṃ tatrāsthā tu śatatrayam .. 159.43 ..
10.0.d:
शरीरावयवैर्युक्तो ह्यङ्गप्रत्यङ्गसंयुतः .
अष्टोत्तरं मर्मशतं तत्रास्था तु शतत्रयम् .. 159.43 ..
10.0.m: Endowed with the bodily parts and equipped with major and minor limbs, / there are one hundred and eight vital points, and three hundred bones,

10.0.s:
sapta śiraḥkapālāni vihitāni svayambhuvā .
tisraḥ koṭyo'rdhakoṭī ca romṇāmaṅgeṣu bhārata .. 159.44 ..
10.0.d:
सप्त शिरःकपालानि विहितानि स्वयम्भुवा .
तिस्रः कोट्योऽर्धकोटी च रोम्णामङ्गेषु भारत .. 159.44 ..
10.0.m: seven cranial bones arranged by the self-manifest [Brahmā], / and three and a half crores of hairs upon the limbs, O Bhārata.

10.0.s:
dvāsaptatisahasrāṇi hṛdayādabhinisṛtāḥ .
hitānāma hi tā nāḍyastāsāṃ madhye śaśiprabhā .. 159.45 ..
10.0.d:
द्वासप्ततिसहस्राणि हृदयादभिनिसृताः .
हितानाम हि ता नाड्यस्तासां मध्ये शशिप्रभा .. 159.45 ..
10.0.m: Seventy-two thousand [channels] branch out from the heart; / these channels are indeed called hitā, and among them is the moon-bright one.

10.0.s:
evaṃ pravartate cakraṃ bhūtagrāme caturvidhe .
utpattiśca vināśaśca bhavataḥ sarvadehinām .. 159.46 ..
10.0.d:
एवं प्रवर्तते चक्रं भूतग्रामे चतुर्विधे .
उत्पत्तिश्च विनाशश्च भवतः सर्वदेहिनाम् .. 159.46 ..
10.0.m: Thus turns the wheel of fourfold classes of living beings; / birth and destruction occur for all embodied souls.

10.0.s:
gatirūrdhvā ca dharmeṇa hyadharmeṇa tvadhogatiḥ .
jāyate sarvavarṇānāṃ svadharmacalanānnṛpa .. 159.47 ..
10.0.d:
गतिरूर्ध्वा च धर्मेण ह्यधर्मेण त्वधोगतिः .
जायते सर्ववर्णानां स्वधर्मचलनान्नृप .. 159.47 ..
10.0.m: An upward course comes through dharma, but a downward course through adharma; / it occurs for all classes, O king, from deviating from one's own duty.

10.0.s:
devatve mānavatve ca dānabhogādikāḥ kriyāḥ .
dṛśyante yā mahārāja tatsarvaṃ karmajaṃ phalam .. 159.48 ..
10.0.d:
देवत्वे मानवत्वे च दानभोगादिकाः क्रियाः .
दृश्यन्ते या महाराज तत्सर्वं कर्मजं फलम् .. 159.48 ..
10.0.m: In divinity and in humanity, acts such as charity and enjoyment / that are seen, O great king, are all fruits born of action.

10.0.s:
svakarma vihite ghore kāmaksodhārjite śubhe .
nimajjennarake ghore yasyottāro na vidyate .. 159.49 ..
10.0.d:
स्वकर्म विहिते घोरे कामक्सोधार्जिते शुभे .
निमज्जेन्नरके घोरे यस्योत्तारो न विद्यते .. 159.49 ..
10.0.m: In the dreadful state caused by one's own karma, acquired through lust and anger [or] auspicious, / one may sink into a dreadful hell from which there is no crossing over.

10.0.s:
uttāraṇāya jantūnāṃ narmadātaṭasaṃsthitam .
evametanmahātīrthaṃ narakeśvaramuttamam .. 159.50 ..
10.0.d:
उत्तारणाय जन्तूनां नर्मदातटसंस्थितम् .
एवमेतन्महातीर्थं नरकेश्वरमुत्तमम् .. 159.50 ..
10.0.m: For the salvation of living beings, situated on the bank of the Narmadā / is this great tīrtha, the supreme Narakeśvara,

10.0.s:
narakāpahaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam .
tattīrthaṃ sarvatīrthānāmuttamaṃ bhuvi durlabham .. 159.51 ..
10.0.d:
नरकापहं महापुण्यं महापातकनाशनम् .
तत्तीर्थं सर्वतीर्थानामुत्तमं भुवि दुर्लभम् .. 159.51 ..
10.0.m: destroyer of hell, immensely meritorious, destroying great sins; / that tīrtha is the best of all tīrthas, hard to attain on earth.

10.0.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ snātvā pūjayeta maheśvaram .
mahāpātakayukto'pi narakaṃ naiva paśyati .. 159.52 ..
10.0.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः स्नात्वा पूजयेत महेश्वरम् .
महापातकयुक्तोऽपि नरकं नैव पश्यति .. 159.52 ..
10.0.m: Having bathed in that tīrtha, whoever worships Maheśvara, / even if possessed of great sins, never sees hell.

10.0.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yo dadyāddhenuṃ vaitaraṇīṃ śubhām .
sa mucyate sukhenaiva vaitaraṇyāṃ na saṃśayaḥ .. 159.53 ..
10.0.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यो दद्याद्धेनुं वैतरणीं शुभाम् .
स मुच्यते सुखेनैव वैतरण्यां न संशयः .. 159.53 ..
10.0.m: Whoever gives an auspicious Vaitaraṇī cow at that tīrtha, / is freed with ease from Vaitaraṇī; there is no doubt.

10.0.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
yamadvāre mahāghore yā sā vaitaraṇī nadī .
kiṃrūpā kiṃpramāṇā sā kathaṃ sā vahati dvija .. 159.54 ..
10.0.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
यमद्वारे महाघोरे या सा वैतरणी नदी .
किंरूपा किंप्रमाणा सा कथं सा वहति द्विज .. 159.54 ..
10.0.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / That river Vaitaraṇī which is at the terrifying gateway of Yama, / what is its form, what is its extent, and how does it flow, O twice-born one?

10.0.s:
kathaṃ tasyāḥ pramucyante keṣāṃ vāsastu saṃtatam .
keṣāṃ tu sānukūlā sā hyetadvistarato vada .. 159.55 ..
10.0.d:
कथं तस्याः प्रमुच्यन्ते केषां वासस्तु संततम् .
केषां तु सानुकूला सा ह्येतद्विस्तरतो वद .. 159.55 ..
10.0.m: How are people freed from it, who dwells in it perpetually, / and to whom is it favorable? Tell this in detail.

10.0.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
dharmaputra mahābāho śṛṇu sarvaṃ mayoditam .
yā sā vaitaraṇī nāma yamadvāre mahāsarit .. 159.56 ..
10.0.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
धर्मपुत्र महाबाहो शृणु सर्वं मयोदितम् .
या सा वैतरणी नाम यमद्वारे महासरित् .. 159.56 ..
10.0.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / O son of Dharma, O mighty-armed one, hear everything spoken by me / concerning that great river named Vaitaraṇī at the gateway of Yama.

10.0.s:
agādhā pārarahitā dṛṣṭamātrā bhayāvahā .
pūyaśoṇitatoyā sā māṃsakardamanirmitā .. 159.57 ..
10.0.d:
अगाधा पाररहिता दृष्टमात्रा भयावहा .
पूयशोणिततोया सा मांसकर्दमनिर्मिता .. 159.57 ..
10.0.m: It is bottomless, boundless, and terrifying just to behold. / Its waters are pus and blood, and it is made of mire of flesh.

10.0.s:
tattoyaṃ bhramate tūrṇaṃ tāpīmadhye ghṛtaṃ yathā .
kṛmibhiḥ saṅkulaṃ pūyaṃ vajratuṇḍairayomukhaiḥ .. 159.58 ..
10.0.d:
तत्तोयं भ्रमते तूर्णं तापीमध्ये घृतं यथा .
कृमिभिः सङ्कुलं पूयं वज्रतुण्डैरयोमुखैः .. 159.58 ..
10.0.m: Its water swirls rapidly, like ghee in a frying pan; / it is full of pus and teeming with worms having adamantine beaks and iron mouths,

10.0.s:
śiśumāraiśca makarairvajrakartarisaṃyutaiḥ .
anyaiśca jalajīvaiḥ sā suhiṃsrairmarmabhedibhiḥ .. 159.59 ..
10.0.d:
शिशुमारैश्च मकरैर्वज्रकर्तरिसंयुतैः .
अन्यैश्च जलजीवैः सा सुहिंस्रैर्मर्मभेदिभिः .. 159.59 ..
10.0.m: and with dolphins and crocodiles equipped with adamantine shears, / and with other water creatures that are intensely violent and pierce the vital points.

10.0.s:
tapanti dvādaśādityāḥ pralayānta ivolbaṇāḥ .
patanti tatra vai martyāḥ krandanto bhṛśadāruṇam .. 159.60 ..
10.0.d:
तपन्ति द्वादशादित्याः प्रलयान्त इवोल्बणाः .
पतन्ति तत्र वै मर्त्याः क्रन्दन्तो भृशदारुणम् .. 159.60 ..
10.0.m: Twelve suns blaze fiercely as if at the end of a cosmic dissolution. / Mortals fall in there, weeping intensely and dreadfully,

10.0.s:
hā bhrātaḥ putra hā mātaḥ pralapanti muhurmuhuḥ .
asipattravane ghore patantaṃ yo'bhirakṣati .. 159.61 ..
10.0.d:
हा भ्रातः पुत्र हा मातः प्रलपन्ति मुहुर्मुहुः .
असिपत्त्रवने घोरे पतन्तं योऽभिरक्षति .. 159.61 ..
10.0.m: lamenting again and again, ‘O brother! O son! O mother!’ / Who can protect the one falling into the terrifying Asipattravana?

10.0.s:
prataranti nimajjanti glāniṃ gacchanti jantavaḥ .
caturvidhaiḥ prāṇigaṇairdraṣṭavyā sā mahānadī .. 159.62 ..
10.0.d:
प्रतरन्ति निमज्जन्ति ग्लानिं गच्छन्ति जन्तवः .
चतुर्विधैः प्राणिगणैर्द्रष्टव्या सा महानदी .. 159.62 ..
10.0.m: Creatures swim, sink, and become exhausted. / That great river must be faced by the four types of living beings.

10.0.s:
taranti tasyāṃ saddānairanyathā tu patanti te .
mātaraṃ ye na manyante hyācāryaṃ gurumeva ca .. 159.63 ..
10.0.d:
तरन्ति तस्यां सद्दानैरन्यथा तु पतन्ति ते .
मातरं ये न मन्यन्ते ह्याचार्यं गुरुमेव च .. 159.63 ..
10.0.m: They cross over it through noble gifts; otherwise they fall. / Those who do not respect their mother, teacher, and guru,

10.0.s:
avajānanti mūḍhā ye teṣāṃ vāsastu saṃtatam .
pativratāṃ sādhuśīlāmūḍhāṃ dharmeṣu niścalām .. 159.64 ..
10.0.d:
अवजानन्ति मूढा ये तेषां वासस्तु संततम् .
पतिव्रतां साधुशीलामूढां धर्मेषु निश्चलाम् .. 159.64 ..
10.0.m: the fools who despise them—theirs is a perpetual dwelling [there]. / A devoted wife of virtuous conduct, legally married and steadfast in duties—

10.0.s:
parityajanti ye pāpāḥ saṃtataṃ tu vasanti te .
viśvāsapratipannānāṃ svāmimitratapasvinām .. 159.65 ..
10.0.d:
परित्यजन्ति ये पापाः संततं तु वसन्ति ते .
विश्वासप्रतिपन्नानां स्वामिमित्रतपस्विनाम् .. 159.65 ..
10.0.m: those wicked men who abandon [her] dwell [there] perpetually. / Of those who have placed their trust—masters, friends, ascetics,

10.0.s:
strībālavṛddhadīnānāṃ chidramanveṣayanti ye .
pacyante tatra madhye vai krandamānāḥ supāpinaḥ .. 159.66 ..
10.0.d:
स्त्रीबालवृद्धदीनानां छिद्रमन्वेषयन्ति ये .
पच्यन्ते तत्र मध्ये वै क्रन्दमानाः सुपापिनः .. 159.66 ..
10.0.m: women, children, the elderly, and the helpless—those who seek their vulnerabilities, / those great sinners are boiled in the middle of it, crying out.

10.0.s:
śrāntaṃ bubhukṣitaṃ vipraṃ yo vighnayati durmatiḥ .
kṛmibhirbhakṣyate tatra yāvatkalpaśatatrayam .. 159.67 ..
10.0.d:
श्रान्तं बुभुक्षितं विप्रं यो विघ्नयति दुर्मतिः .
कृमिभिर्भक्ष्यते तत्र यावत्कल्पशतत्रयम् .. 159.67 ..
10.0.m: The evil-minded one who obstructs an exhausted, hungry brahmin / is eaten there by worms for three hundred kalpas.

10.0.s:
brāhmaṇāya pratiśrutya yo dānaṃ na prayacchati .
āhūya nāsti yo brūte tasya vāsastu saṃtatam .. 159.68 ..
10.0.d:
ब्राह्मणाय प्रतिश्रुत्य यो दानं न प्रयच्छति .
आहूय नास्ति यो ब्रूते तस्य वासस्तु संततम् .. 159.68 ..
10.0.m: He who promises a gift to a brahmin and does not give it, / or summons him and says ‘There is nothing,’ dwells there perpetually.

10.0.s:
agnido garadaścaiva rājagāmī ca paiśunī .
kathābhaṅgakaraścaiva kūṭasākṣī ca madyapaḥ .. 159.69 ..
10.0.d:
अग्निदो गरदश्चैव राजगामी च पैशुनी .
कथाभङ्गकरश्चैव कूटसाक्षी च मद्यपः .. 159.69 ..
10.0.m: An arsonist, a poisoner, an informer to the king, a slanderer, / an interrupter of sacred discourse, a false witness, and a drinker of liquor,

10.0.s:
vajravidhvaṃsakaścaiva svayaṃdattāpahārakaḥ .
sukṣetrasetubhedī ca paradārapradharṣakaḥ .. 159.70 ..
10.0.d:
वज्रविध्वंसकश्चैव स्वयंदत्तापहारकः .
सुक्षेत्रसेतुभेदी च परदारप्रधर्षकः .. 159.70 ..
10.0.m: a destroyer of thunderbolts, a taker of what was given by oneself, / a destroyer of dikes in good fields, and a violator of another's wife,

10.0.s:
brāhmaṇo rasavikretā vṛṣalīpatireva ca .
gokulasya tṛṣārtasya pālībhedaṃ karoti yaḥ .. 159.71 ..
10.0.d:
ब्राह्मणो रसविक्रेता वृषलीपतिरेव च .
गोकुलस्य तृषार्तस्य पालीभेदं करोति यः .. 159.71 ..
10.0.m: a brahmin who sells liquids, a husband of a Śūdra woman, / and he who breaks the water embankment of thirsty cattle,

10.0.s:
kanyābhidūṣakaścaiva dānaṃ dattvā tu tāpakaḥ .
śūdrastu kapilāpānī brāhmaṇo māṃsabhojanī .. 159.72 ..
10.0.d:
कन्याभिदूषकश्चैव दानं दत्त्वा तु तापकः .
शूद्रस्तु कपिलापानी ब्राह्मणो मांसभोजनी .. 159.72 ..
10.0.m: a corrupter of maidens, one who regrets having given a gift, / a Śūdra who drinks milk from a tawny cow, a brahmin who eats meat—

10.0.s:
ete vasanti satataṃ mā vicāraṃ kṛthā nṛpa .
sānukūlā bhavedyena tacchṛṇuṣva narādhipa .. 159.73 ..
10.0.d:
एते वसन्ति सततं मा विचारं कृथा नृप .
सानुकूला भवेद्येन तच्छृणुष्व नराधिप .. 159.73 ..
10.0.m: these dwell [there] continually; do not doubt it, O king. / Hear that by which it may become favorable, O ruler of men.

10.0.s:
ayane viṣuve caiva vyatīpāte dinakṣaye .
anyeṣu puṇyakāleṣu dīyate dānamuttamam .. 159.74 ..
10.0.d:
अयने विषुवे चैव व्यतीपाते दिनक्षये .
अन्येषु पुण्यकालेषु दीयते दानमुत्तमम् .. 159.74 ..
10.0.m:
At a solstice, at an equinox, at a vyatīpāta, on the day of a new moon,
and at other sacred times, this supreme gift is given.

10.0.s:
kṛṣṇāṃ vā pāṭalāṃ vāpi kuryādvaitaraṇīṃ śubhām .
svarṇaśṛṅgīṃ rūpyakhurāṃ kāṃsyapātrasya dohinīm .. 159.75 ..
10.0.d:
कृष्णां वा पाटलां वापि कुर्याद्वैतरणीं शुभाम् .
स्वर्णशृङ्गीं रूप्यखुरां कांस्यपात्रस्य दोहिनीम् .. 159.75 ..
10.0.m:
One should make an auspicious Vaitaraṇī cow, either black or reddish-brown,
with golden horns, silver hooves, and milkable into a bronze vessel,

10.0.s:
kṛṣṇavastrayugācchannāṃ saptadhānyasamanvitām .
kuryātsadroṇaśikhara āsīnāṃ tāmrabhājane .. 159.76 ..
10.0.d:
कृष्णवस्त्रयुगाच्छन्नां सप्तधान्यसमन्विताम् .
कुर्यात्सद्रोणशिखर आसीनां ताम्रभाजने .. 159.76 ..
10.0.m:
covered with a pair of black garments, accompanied by the seven grains,
seated upon a copper vessel topped with a droṇa [of grain].

10.0.s:
yamaṃ haimaṃ prakurvīta lohadaṇḍasamanvitam .
ikṣudaṇḍamayaṃ baddhvā hyuḍupaṃ paṭṭabandhanaiḥ .. 159.77 ..
10.0.d:
यमं हैमं प्रकुर्वीत लोहदण्डसमन्वितम् .
इक्षुदण्डमयं बद्ध्वा ह्युडुपं पट्टबन्धनैः .. 159.77 ..
10.0.m:
One should make a golden Yama equipped with an iron rod,
and having constructed a raft made of sugarcanes bound with silken cords,

10.0.s:
uḍupopari tāṃ dhenuṃ sūryadehasamudbhavām .
kṛtvā prakalpayedvidvāñchattropānadyugānvitām .. 159.78 ..
10.0.d:
उडुपोपरि तां धेनुं सूर्यदेहसमुद्भवाम् .
कृत्वा प्रकल्पयेद्विद्वाञ्छत्त्रोपानद्युगान्विताम् .. 159.78 ..
10.0.m:
the wise man should place that cow, born from the body of the sun,
upon the raft, equipped with an umbrella and a pair of sandals.

10.0.s:
aṅgulīyakavāsāṃsi brāhmaṇāya nivedayet .
imamuccārayenmantraṃ saṃgṛhyāsyāśca pucchakam .. 159.79 ..
10.0.d:
अङ्गुलीयकवासांसि ब्राह्मणाय निवेदयेत् .
इममुच्चारयेन्मन्त्रं संगृह्यास्याश्च पुच्छकम् .. 159.79 ..
10.0.m:
He should present a finger-ring and garments to a brahmin,
and, taking hold of the cow's tail, he should recite this mantra:

10.0.s:
oṃ yamadvāre mahāghore yā sā vaitaraṇī nadī .
tartukāmo dadāmyenāṃ tubhyaṃ vaitaraṇi namaḥ .
ityadhivāsanamantraḥ .. 159.80 ..
10.0.d:
ओं यमद्वारे महाघोरे या सा वैतरणी नदी .
तर्तुकामो ददाम्येनां तुभ्यं वैतरणि नमः .
इत्यधिवासनमन्त्रः .. 159.80 ..
10.0.m:
“Oṃ. The river that is the Vaitaraṇī at the terrible door of Yama—
desiring to cross it, I give this [cow]; homage to you, O Vaitaraṇī!”
Such is the mantra of preliminary consecration.

10.0.s:
gāvo me cāgrataḥ santu gāvo me santu pṛṣṭhataḥ .
gāvo me hṛdaye santu gavāṃ madhye vasāmyaham .. 159.81 ..
10.0.d:
गावो मे चाग्रतः सन्तु गावो मे सन्तु पृष्ठतः .
गावो मे हृदये सन्तु गवां मध्ये वसाम्यहम् .. 159.81 ..
10.0.m:
“May cows be in front of me; may cows be behind me;
may cows be in my heart; I dwell in the midst of cows.”

10.0.s:
oṃ viṣṇurūpa dvijaśreṣṭha bhūdeva paṅktipāvana .
sadakṣiṇā mayā dattā tubhyaṃ vaitaraṇi namaḥ .
iti dānamantraḥ .. 159.82 ..
10.0.d:
ओं विष्णुरूप द्विजश्रेष्ठ भूदेव पङ्क्तिपावन .
सदक्षिणा मया दत्ता तुभ्यं वैतरणि नमः .
इति दानमन्त्रः .. 159.82 ..
10.0.m:
“Oṃ. You who are a form of Viṣṇu, best of the twice-born, earthly god, sanctifier of the row,
this [cow] is given by me with a sacrificial fee; homage to you, O Vaitaraṇī!”
Such is the gift mantra.

10.0.s:
brāhmaṇaṃ dharmarājaṃ ca dhenuṃ vaitaraṇīṃ śivām .
sarvaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya brāhmaṇāya nivedayet .. 159.83 ..
10.0.d:
ब्राह्मणं धर्मराजं च धेनुं वैतरणीं शिवाम् .
सर्वं प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य ब्राह्मणाय निवेदयेत् .. 159.83 ..
10.0.m:
Having circumambulated the brahmin, Dharmarāja, and the auspicious Vaitaraṇī cow,
he should present everything to the brahmin.

10.0.s: pucchaṃ saṃgṛhya surabheragre kṛtvā dvijaṃ tataḥ .. 159.84 ..
10.0.d: पुच्छं संगृह्य सुरभेरग्रे कृत्वा द्विजं ततः .. 159.84 ..
10.0.m: Taking hold of the cow’s tail, having placed the twice-born in front, then:

10.0.s:
dhenuke tvaṃ pratīkṣasva yamadvāre mahābhaye .
uttitīrṣurahaṃ dheno vaitaraṇyai namo'stu te .
ityanuvrajamantraḥ .. 159.85 ..
10.0.d:
धेनुके त्वं प्रतीक्षस्व यमद्वारे महाभये .
उत्तितीर्षुरहं धेनो वैतरण्यै नमोऽस्तु ते .
इत्यनुव्रजमन्त्रः .. 159.85 ..
10.0.m:
“O cow, wait for me at the gateway of Yama, which brings great fear!
I wish to cross over, O cow; homage be to you, Vaitaraṇī!”
Such is the mantra for following after.

10.0.s:
anuvrajeta gacchantaṃ sarvaṃ tasya gṛhaṃ nayet .
evaṃ kṛte mahīpāla saritsyātsukhavāhinī .. 159.86 ..
10.0.d:
अनुव्रजेत गच्छन्तं सर्वं तस्य गृहं नयेत् .
एवं कृते महीपाल सरित्स्यात्सुखवाहिनी .. 159.86 ..
10.0.m:
He should follow him as he departs, and bring everything to his house.
When this is done, O protector of the earth, the river flows pleasantly.

10.0.s:
tārayate tayā dhenvā sā sarijjalavāhinī .
sarvānkāmānavāpnoti ye divyā ye ca mānuṣāḥ .. 159.87 ..
10.0.d:
तारयते तया धेन्वा सा सरिज्जलवाहिनी .
सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति ये दिव्या ये च मानुषाः .. 159.87 ..
10.0.m:
By means of that cow, that river which flows with water carries him across.
He obtains all desires, both divine and human.

10.0.s:
rogī rogādvimuktaḥ syācchāmyanti paramāpadaḥ .
svasthe sahasraguṇitamāture śatasaṃmitam .. 159.88 ..
10.0.d:
रोगी रोगाद्विमुक्तः स्याच्छाम्यन्ति परमापदः .
स्वस्थे सहस्रगुणितमातुरे शतसंमितम् .. 159.88 ..
10.0.m:
A sick man would be freed from illness; the greatest misfortunes are pacified.
When healthy, [the gift's fruit] is multiplied a thousandfold; when sick, it is reckoned a hundredfold.

10.0.s:
mṛtasyaiva tu yaddānaṃ parokṣe tatsamaṃ smṛtam .
svahastena tato deyaṃ mṛte kaḥ kasya dāsyati .
iti matvā mahārāja svadattaṃ syānmahāphalam .. 159.89 ..
10.0.d:
मृतस्यैव तु यद्दानं परोक्षे तत्समं स्मृतम् .
स्वहस्तेन ततो देयं मृते कः कस्य दास्यति .
इति मत्वा महाराज स्वदत्तं स्यान्महाफलम् .. 159.89 ..
10.0.m:
The gift given on behalf of a deceased person in their absence is remembered as equal [to ordinary fruit].
Therefore, one should give with one's own hand: when one is dead, who will give to whom?
Considering this, O great king, what is given by oneself bears great fruit.

10.0.s:
ityevamuktaṃ tava dharmasūno dānaṃ mayā vaitaraṇīsamuttham .
śṛṇoti bhaktyā paṭhatīha samyaksa yāti viṣṇoḥ padamaprameyam .. 159.90 ..
10.0.d:
इत्येवमुक्तं तव धर्मसूनो दानं मया वैतरणीसमुत्थम् .
शृणोति भक्त्या पठतीह सम्यक्स याति विष्णोः पदमप्रमेयम् .. 159.90 ..
10.0.m:
Thus has the gift pertaining to the Vaitaraṇī been spoken to you, O son of Dharma.
Whoever hears or recites this properly with devotion goes to the unmeasurable abode of Viṣṇu.

10.0.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
prāpte cāśvayuje māsi tasminkṛṣṇā caturdaśī .
snātvā kṛtvā tataḥ śrāddhaṃ sampūjya ca maheśvaram .. 159.91 ..
10.0.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
प्राप्ते चाश्वयुजे मासि तस्मिन्कृष्णा चतुर्दशी .
स्नात्वा कृत्वा ततः श्राद्धं सम्पूज्य च महेश्वरम् .. 159.91 ..
10.0.m:
The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said:
When the month of Āśvayuja arrives, on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight,
having bathed, performed the ancestral offering, and worshipped the great lord,

10.0.s:
pitṛbhyo dīyate dānaṃ bhaktiśraddhāsamanvitaiḥ .
paścājjāgaraṇaṃ kuryātsatkathāśravaṇādibhiḥ .. 159.92 ..
10.0.d:
पितृभ्यो दीयते दानं भक्तिश्रद्धासमन्वितैः .
पश्चाज्जागरणं कुर्यात्सत्कथाश्रवणादिभिः .. 159.92 ..
10.0.m:
gifts are given to the ancestors by those endowed with devotion and faith.
Afterwards, one should keep a vigil by listening to virtuous stories and the like.

10.0.s:
tataḥ prabhātasamaye snātvā vai narmadājale .
tarpaṇaṃ vidhivatkṛtvā pitḥṇāṃ devapūrvakam .. 159.93 ..
10.0.d:
ततः प्रभातसमये स्नात्वा वै नर्मदाजले .
तर्पणं विधिवत्कृत्वा पित्ःणां देवपूर्वकम् .. 159.93 ..
10.0.m:
Then, at dawn, having bathed in the waters of the Narmadā
and duly made water-offerings to the ancestors, preceded by the gods,

10.0.s:
sauvarṇe ghṛtasaṃyuktaṃ dīpaṃ dadyāddvijātaye .
paścātsaṃbhojayedviprān svayaṃ caiva vimatsaraḥ .. 159.94 ..
10.0.d:
सौवर्णे घृतसंयुक्तं दीपं दद्याद्द्विजातये .
पश्चात्संभोजयेद्विप्रान् स्वयं चैव विमत्सरः .. 159.94 ..
10.0.m:
one should give to a twice-born a lamp filled with ghee in a golden vessel.
Afterwards, free from envy, he should feed the brahmins and himself.

10.0.s:
evaṃ kṛte naraśreṣṭha na janturnarakaṃ vrajet .
avaśyameva manujairdraṣṭavyā nārakī sthitiḥ .. 159.95 ..
10.0.d:
एवं कृते नरश्रेष्ठ न जन्तुर्नरकं व्रजेत् .
अवश्यमेव मनुजैर्द्रष्टव्या नारकी स्थितिः .. 159.95 ..
10.0.m:
When this is done, O best of men, a living being does not go to hell.
A state of hell must inevitably be seen by mortals,

10.0.s:
anena vidhinā kṛtvā na paśyennarakānnaraḥ .
tatra tīrthe mṛtānāṃ tu narāṇāṃ vidhinā nṛpa .. 159.96 ..
10.0.d:
अनेन विधिना कृत्वा न पश्येन्नरकान्नरः .
तत्र तीर्थे मृतानां तु नराणां विधिना नृप .. 159.96 ..
10.0.m:
yet performing [it] by this rite, a man does not see the hells.
For men who die at that sacred ford according to the rule, O king,

10.0.s:
manvantaraṃ śive loke vāso bhavati durlabhe .
vimānenārkavarṇena kiṃkiṇīśataśobhinā .. 159.97 ..
10.0.d:
मन्वन्तरं शिवे लोके वासो भवति दुर्लभे .
विमानेनार्कवर्णेन किंकिणीशतशोभिना .. 159.97 ..
10.0.m:
their residence in the rarely attainable world of Śiva lasts for a manvantara.
In an aerial chariot bright as the sun, adorned with hundreds of small bells,

10.0.s:
sa gacchati mahābhāga sevyamāno'psarogaṇaiḥ .
bhunakti vividhānbhogānuktakālaṃ na saṃśayaḥ .. 159.98 ..
10.0.d:
स गच्छति महाभाग सेव्यमानोऽप्सरोगणैः .
भुनक्ति विविधान्भोगानुक्तकालं न संशयः .. 159.98 ..
10.0.m:
he travels, O fortunate one, served by hosts of apsarases;
he enjoys various pleasures for the stated time, without doubt.

10.0.s:
pūrṇe caiva tataḥ kāla iha mānuṣyatāṃ gataḥ .
sarvavyādhivinirmukto jīvecca śaradāṃ śatam .. 159.99 ..
10.0.d:
पूर्णे चैव ततः काल इह मानुष्यतां गतः .
सर्वव्याधिविनिर्मुक्तो जीवेच्च शरदां शतम् .. 159.99 ..
10.0.m:
And when that time is complete, having attained human birth here,
freed from all illnesses, he lives for a hundred autumns.

10.0.s:
prāpya cāśvayuje māsi kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśīm .
ahorātroṣito bhūtvā pūjayitvā maheśvaram .
mahāpātakayukto'pi mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 159.100 ..
10.0.d:
प्राप्य चाश्वयुजे मासि कृष्णपक्षे चतुर्दशीम् .
अहोरात्रोषितो भूत्वा पूजयित्वा महेश्वरम् .
महापातकयुक्तोऽपि मुच्यते नात्र संशयः .. 159.100 ..
10.0.m:
Reaching the fourteenth day in the dark fortnight of the month of Āśvayuja,
having fasted for a day and night and worshipped the great lord,
even if guilty of a great sin, he is freed—there is no doubt about this.

10.0.s:
aṣṭāviṃśatikoṭyo vai narakāṇāṃ yudhiṣṭhira .
vimuktā narakairduḥkhaiḥ śivalokaṃ vrajanti te .. 159.101 ..
10.0.d:
अष्टाविंशतिकोट्यो वै नरकाणां युधिष्ठिर .
विमुक्ता नरकैर्दुःखैः शिवलोकं व्रजन्ति ते .. 159.101 ..
10.0.m:
There are indeed twenty-eight crores of hells, O Yudhiṣṭhira;
freed from the sufferings of hell, they go to the world of Śiva.

10.0.s:
tatra bhuktvā mahābhogāndivyaiśvaryasamanvitān .
labhante mānuṣaṃ janma durlabhaṃ bhuvi mānavāḥ .. 159.102 ..
.. iti śrīskande mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe'narakeśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmaikonaṣaṣṭyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
10.0.d:
तत्र भुक्त्वा महाभोगान्दिव्यैश्वर्यसमन्वितान् .
लभन्ते मानुषं जन्म दुर्लभं भुवि मानवाः .. 159.102 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कन्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डेऽनरकेश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामैकोनषष्ट्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः ..
10.0.m:
Having enjoyed great pleasures there, endowed with divine sovereignty,
those mortals attain human birth on earth, which is difficult to attain.
Thus ends the one hundred fifty-ninth chapter, entitled "The Description of the Māhātmya of the Anarakeśvara Sacred Ford," in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth Avantī section of the Skandamahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

11.0.s:
.. skaṃda uvāca .. ..
śṛṇu vātāpi saṃhartaḥ kāśyāṃ pātakataṃkinī ..
padmakalpe tu yā vṛttā damanasya dvijanmanaḥ ..1..
bhāradvājasya tanayo damano nāma nāmataḥ ..
kṛtamauṃjīvidhiḥ sotha vidyājātaṃ pragṛhya ca .. 2 ..
saṃsāraduḥkhabahulaṃ jīvitaṃ cāpi caṃcalam ..
vijñāya damano vidvānnirjagāma gṛhānnijāt .. 3 ..
kāṃciddiśaṃ samālaṃbya nirvedaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ ..
pratyāśramaṃ pratinagaṃ pratyabdhi pratikānanam .. 4 ..
pratitīrthaṃ pratinadi sa babhrāma tapoyutaḥ ..
yāvaṃtyāyatanānīha tiṣṭhaṃti parito bhuvam ..5..
adhyuvāsa sa tāvaṃti saṃyateṃdriyamānasaḥ ..
paraṃ na manasaḥ sthairyaṃ kvāpi prāpi ca tena vai .. 6 ..
manorathopadeṣṭā ca kutracitkvāpi nekṣitaḥ ..
kadāciddaivayogātsa damano nāma tāpasaḥ ..7..
revātaṭe niraikṣiṣṭa tīrthaṃ cāmarakaṃṭakam ..
mahadāyatanaṃ puṇyamoṃkārasyāpi tatra vai ..8..
dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭamanā āsīccetaḥ sthairyamavāpa ha ..
atha pāśupatāṃstatra sa nirīkṣya tapodhanān .. 9 ..
11.0.d:
.. स्कंद उवाच .. ..
शृणु वातापि संहर्तः काश्यां पातकतंकिनी ..
पद्मकल्पे तु या वृत्ता दमनस्य द्विजन्मनः ..1..
भारद्वाजस्य तनयो दमनो नाम नामतः ..
कृतमौंजीविधिः सोथ विद्याजातं प्रगृह्य च .. 2 ..
संसारदुःखबहुलं जीवितं चापि चंचलम् ..
विज्ञाय दमनो विद्वान्निर्जगाम गृहान्निजात् .. 3 ..
कांचिद्दिशं समालंब्य निर्वेदं परमं गतः ..
प्रत्याश्रमं प्रतिनगं प्रत्यब्धि प्रतिकाननम् .. 4 ..
प्रतितीर्थं प्रतिनदि स बभ्राम तपोयुतः ..

11.0.m: Skanda said: / Hear, O slayer of Vātāpi, of [the river] that removes sins in Kāśī, / which occurred in the Padma Kalpa regarding the twice-born Damana. / He was the son of Bhāradvāja, named Damana by name. / Having performed the ceremony of the muñja belt and acquired the body of knowledge, / realizing that life is full of the sorrows of saṃsāra and also fickle, / the wise Damana departed from his own house. / Setting out in a certain direction, having attained supreme detachment, / at every hermitage, at every mountain, at every ocean, at every forest, / at every sacred ford, at every river, he wandered, engaged in austerity. / Whatever shrines exist here across the earth, / he dwelled at that many, with his senses and mind restrained. / Yet no steadfastness of mind was attained by him anywhere, / nor was a teacher of his desire seen anywhere at all. / Then, once by the course of destiny, that ascetic named Damana / beheld on the bank of the Revā the sacred ford of Amarakaṇṭaka / and also the great sacred shrine of Oṃkāra there. / Seeing it, he became joyful at heart and attained steadfastness of mind. / Then, beholding the Pāśupatas there, rich in austerity,
their bodies adorned with sacred ash, having performed the worship of the liṅga,
their bodily maintenance regulated, having engaged in contemplation of the Āgamas,
sitting at ease before him, unswerving in mind,
he bowed and sat down there in the presence of their teacher,
his two hands folded, his neck bent down in reverence.
Then the Pāśupata teacher, the great sage named Garga,
overcome by old age, his body emaciated through austerity,
intent on the worship of Śambhu, foremost among all ascetics,
questioned Damana thus: “Who are you, and why have you come here?
Though young, you are dispassionate; whence is this? Tell, O excellent one.”
Having heard this [inquiry] given with affection, Damana said:
“O venerable Pāśupata teacher, lover of the worship of the Omniscient One,
I shall tell you truly the activity of my own mind.
I am an heir of a brahmin, having laboured in the Vedas and Śāstras.
Knowing the vanity of saṃsāra, I took resort in forest-dwelling.
Desiring great perfection with this very body,

thousands of divine herbs were successfully prepared by me;

steadfastness of mind has been reached, as if by one who has attained perfection.

Garga said:
If you desire accomplishment even in this very body,
then listen attentively, and I shall tell you.
In the great sacred field Avimukta, which grants all accomplishments to the virtuous,
the supreme mine of the jewels known as duty, wealth, pleasure, and liberation,
to all creatures of every action who have taken refuge [there],
it is like a lamp to moths, a great elephant to the mass of darkness,
a forest fire to the tree of past actions, a submarine fire to the ocean of mundane existence,
an ocean of milk to the goddess of liberation, a meeting-place of happiness,
the bestower of supreme awakening to those asleep in a long slumber,
a roadside shade-tree to living beings exhausted by wandering to and fro,
the wielder of the thunderbolt against the mountain of great sins accumulated over many births,
the producer of supreme welfare for men who merely utter its name,
the supreme abode of the Lord of the Universe, the boundary between heaven and liberation,
whose surface is perpetually washed by the surging waves of the River of Heaven—
in such a great sacred field, which removes the whole flood of sorrow,
I shall tell you, O wise one, what happened right before my eyes.
